summary: Elevated chat priming latency after runtime 1.7 migration (increased time-to-first-token)
description: Issue summary: After the 1.7 runtime migration (rolled out to Dedicated clusters in us-east on 2025-02-09), LinguaWorks reported elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat-completion streams. Impact: interactive chat experiences are seeing 600ms-2.2s additional latency on first token causing user-facing slow initial responses and some timeouts for low-latency SLAs. Scope: observed across multiple models on the customer's dedicated pool and correlated with runtime rollout window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LinguaWorks dedicated API key against prod us-east endpoint
2) Start a fresh chat session with a ~900-token system prompt and an initial user message
3) Enable streaming and measure time from request received at gateway to first token emitted (TTFB)
4) Repeat for several sessions and compare against baseline measurements from 2025-02-08
logs: 2025-02-10T10:12:03Z DEBUG runtime request_id=gw_8f3 prefill_kv_size=912 tokens priming_start
investigation_notes: Initial triage: SRE confirmed latency spike aligns with 1.7 rollout to customer's dedicated pool (rollout started 2025-02-09 22:00 UTC).
Hypothesis A: Attention kernel swap in 1.7 introduced a priming path that performs a synchronous KV prefill for large system prompts, adding ~500-900ms per request for some sequences.
Hypothesis B: Connection/streaming handshake changes (keepalive/pipelining) cause additional TLS renegotiation for some long-prefill requests leading to sporadic first-token delays.
Metric checks: Increased percentiles on 'first_token_latency_ms' around rollout window; request tracing shows 'prefill_kv_priming' span increased in p50/p95.
Reproduction: Internal repro on smaller dedicated cluster reproduces 700ms added TTFB when system prompt >800 tokens and streaming enabled (matches customer report).
Cross-links: See INT-2331 where engine team observed increased synchronous work in attention_v2 kernel under large prefix sizes.
Temporary mitigation tested: Enabled pre-warm caching flag (runtime toggle) for one customer node reduced TTFB back to baseline in canary tests.
comments: 2025-02-10 11:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reports median TTFB ~1.1s (baseline ~250ms). Customer requests urgent mitigation because this affects demo SLAs.
2025-02-10 11:20 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Correlated with 1.7 rollout; opening runtime investigation with engine team. Added logs and traces.

2025-02-10 13:40 - Engine (Marta Gomez): Noted attention_v2 kernel added synchronous KV normalization step. Draft PR to make normalization async: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4590
2025-02-10 16:10 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer accepted short-term workaround: pin model route to runtime-1.6-compatible variant and enable pre-warm flag. Requested ETA for permanent fix.
2025-02-11 09:30 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Canary patch rolled to 2 nodes with async normalization; observed p95 TTFB drop from 2.2s -> 340ms for large prompts. Monitoring in progress.
resolution: Workaround: Applied customer-scoped mitigation by routing LinguaWorks traffic to a runtime-1.6-compatible model variant and toggling pre-warm KV cache on their dedicated pool. Permanent fix: engine team merged async-normalization patch in PR #4590; rollout scheduled as hotfix to dedicated clusters in us-east on 2025-02-13 with canary gating. Follow-ups: update runbook to include pre-warm toggle for large-prefix workloads, add automated perf regression test for system prompts >800 tokens, notify customers in affected cohorts and include patch rollout notes in release changelog.
follow_up_actions: 1) Roll out hotfix to all dedicated nodes in us-east after canary success (owner: Marta Gomez, ETA: 2025-02-13)
2) Add automated e2e test explaining system-prompt priming across streaming paths (owner: QA-inference)
3) Update operational runbook with pre-warm toggle and detection alert (owner: SRE)
4) Send customer-facing summary and mitigation timeline to LinguaWorks CS contact (owner: Support)
